investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-06T12:31–12:32Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm backend at the AWS ELB endpoint during POST /api/agents. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unverifiable. This is an eval-detected infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the internal AWS ELB-backed service at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint that handles POST /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api layer at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents as its first step (evidenced by the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 calling createAgent with machineType "remote"), and all three checks received the same 502 bad_gateway response with error code "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning". Because the gateway was unreachable, no agent was created, no VM was assigned, and no evidence could be collected, causing complete contract failure. The root cause is a connectivity or availability problem at the swarm gateway layer, not in the eval runner or contract definitions themselves.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents as its first step, which proxies to that ELB. The gateway returned a 502 before any agent could be created, causing all three sibling checks to fail with the same error message and produce zero evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability failure localized to the swarm gateway / agent provisioning path; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 683 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 683 minutes old at evaluation time, more than double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the staleness of the published snapshot JSON, not to any broader website or infrastructure outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot served at eval time was 683 minutes old, meaning the workflow either failed, was skipped, was disabled, or was blocked for approximately 11+ hours before the eval ran at 2026-09-06T12:32:06Z. This is an eval-detected workflow scheduling or execution gap; no evidence of a user-facing website outage is present, as all sibling page checks passed.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 683' — the sole violated assertion in the contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482: { "path": "snapshotAgeMinutes", "max": 300 }).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=683, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and is structurally valid but is stale by 383 minutes beyond the allowed threshold.

expected-output.contract: the snapshotAgeMinutes assertion requires max 300; all other 10 assertions (schemaVersion, overall, generatedAtPresent, source, featureCount, totalsFeatures, hasLiveSource, hasNonUnknownFeatureData, snapshotUrl, maxAgeMinutes) passed.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks returned status=pass, confirming the public website is reachable and the failure is isolated to the snapshot freshness.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check is registered as required=false, statusImpact='informational', staleAfterMinutes=360 — the registry staleAfterMinutes (360) is itself higher than the contract max (300), indicating a potential configuration inconsistency between the registry and the expected-output contract.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2170: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from statusSnapshotEvidence(payload), confirming the age value is computed from the live-fetched payload, not a cached eval artifact.
possibleCauses: Most likely — GitHub Actions snapshot-publishing workflow did not execute within the last 300 minutes: the snapshot source field is 'github-actions' and snapshotAgeMinutes=683, indicating the workflow that writes status.json to GitHub Pages has not completed a successful run in over 11 hours.

Secondary — GitHub Actions workflow was scheduled but failed mid-run (e.g., permissions error, Pages deployment failure, or runner quota exhaustion), leaving the previously published stale snapshot in place.
Secondary — GitHub Actions workflow schedule was paused, disabled, or its cron trigger was removed or misconfigured, causing it to stop running entirely.

Configuration inconsistency (lower confidence) — the registry entry at infra/evals/status/features.json line 383 sets staleAfterMinutes=360, while the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 enforces max 300 for snapshotAgeMinutes. If the workflow ran on the 360-minute registry cadence, a run completing just before the 360-minute mark would still violate the 300-minute contract threshold, though the observed 683-minute age far exceeds both values and points to a missed run rather than a boundary edge case.
